```json
{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "U1: gpfdist sink will be moved to core with minimal refactoring; original code structure preserved to limit regression risk.",
    "U2: Module registry will be backed by a Git repository (not the GitHub REST API) using simple clone/pull/push semantics executed by the admin and container nodes; admin acts as the writer, containers as the readers.",
    "U3: Benchmark will use a representative mix of fan-in and fan-out streams to evaluate horizontal scaling when adding xd-container nodes; results will be published as an internal report rather than as new framework code.",
    "U4: Flo parser endpoint improvements will follow a uniform error response envelope (HTTP status + machine-readable error code + human message) consistent with existing Spring XD REST APIs.",
    "U5: Mail source SSL/TLS support will be implemented by passing through JavaMail Session properties (util:properties bean) into the existing Spring Integration mail adapter, avoiding custom SSL plumbing.",
    "U6: HDFS becomes the default distributed remote location for the module registry; custom-modules.zip will be removed from the YARN distribution artifacts and replaced with a build-time note directing admins to upload via xd-shell/REST.",
    "U7: xd-shell auto-configuration will be implemented via a documented init script location (e.g. /etc/springxd/conf/xd-shell.init) that is replayed at shell startup using the existing 'script' command.",
    "U8: Graceful stream shutdown will be implemented by setting a configurable drain timeout on the message bus, then signalling modules to stop accepting new messages, and only stopping the container once the bus is drained or the timeout elapses."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "A single developer performs all the work (no team coordination overhead included beyond a self-review pass per activity).",
    "One workday equals 8 hours of focused, uninterrupted development work.",
    "The developer is already familiar with the Spring XD codebase, build system (Gradle), and existing test infrastructure, so ramp-up time is not estimated separately.",
    "No large-scale refactoring or new architectural frameworks are introduced; each user story is a focused, additive change.",
    "Each user story bundles design, implementation, unit tests, and integration tests, plus the minimum required documentation update; an extra global integration and release pass is added at the end.",
    "Rackspace infrastructure for U3 is already provisioned or can be provisioned in a single setup pass; cost of the infrastructure itself is out of scope.",
    "Test mail servers (plain and SSL/TLS-enabled IMAP/SMTP) are available locally or via freely accessible test accounts for U5.",
    "The existing Flo parser service is a standalone web application whose endpoints can be modified without breaking the Flo UI.",
    "HDFS is the only distributed remote location supported after U6; NFS-based distributed locations are out of scope.",
    "Effort estimates cover development work only; they do not include code reviews by other developers, stakeholder meetings, or waiting time on external teams."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Architecture and overall design",
      "activity_description": "Produce the high-level design for the increment: decide how the Git-backed module registry (U2), HDFS default (U6), and graceful shutdown (U8) interact with existing XD lifecycle; document key interfaces and configuration changes that cut across user stories.",
      "most_likely_effort": 2
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "U1 - Migrate gpfdist sink to core",
      "activity_description": "Extract the project reactor based gpfdist sink from the spring-xd-modules repository, relocate it under the core Spring XD sources, wire it into the main build, adjust package names, and add unit and integration tests for the relocated module.",
      "most_likely_effort": 6
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "U2 - Centralized GitHub module registry",
      "activity_description": "Implement a Git-backed module registry: admin server pushes uploaded modules to a configured GitHub repository, container nodes clone/pull the registry on startup and on refresh, conflict handling for concurrent admins, and integration tests covering multi-node sync.",
      "most_likely_effort": 10
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "U3 - Benchmark Rabbit on Rackspace",
      "activity_description": "Provision a Rackspace-based XD cluster, define benchmark scenarios (varying number of xd-container nodes, message rates, stream topologies), execute the benchmarks, collect metrics, and produce a written report on scaling behavior.",
      "most_likely_effort": 5
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "U4 - Improve Flo parser error reporting",
      "activity_description": "Review current Flo parser endpoints, redesign the error response format to be consistent and machine-readable, update the affected endpoints, update the Flo UI/client to consume the new format, and add unit and integration tests covering the failure cases.",
      "most_likely_effort": 5
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "U5 - Mail source SSL/TLS support",
      "activity_description": "Extend the Mail source module configuration to accept a util:properties bean for JavaMail properties (SSL/TLS, trust, etc.), wire it into the underlying Spring Integration mail adapter, add tests for IMAPS/SMTPS connections, and document the new configuration.",
      "most_likely_effort": 4
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "U6 - HDFS as default module registry location",
      "activity_description": "Change the default distributed remote module registry location to HDFS, update xd-shell and REST-API upload flows to use HDFS by default, remove custom-modules.zip from the YARN distribution build, and verify that uploading/listing modules works against HDFS.",
      "most_likely_effort": 3
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "U7 - xd-shell auto-configuration via init script",
      "activity_description": "Add support to xd-shell for automatically loading and executing a predefined init script at startup (e.g. /etc/springxd/conf/xd-shell.init), implement discovery of the script location, add tests, and document the convention.",
      "most_likely_effort": 4
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "U8 - Graceful stream shutdown",
      "activity_description": "Implement graceful stream undeployment: add a configurable drain timeout, stop intake of new messages on the source, wait for in-flight messages to reach the sink or DLQ, then stop the container; add unit and integration tests for mid-flight undeploy scenarios.",
      "most_likely_effort": 6
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Cross-feature integration testing",
      "activity_description": "Run end-to-end tests that combine the new features (e.g. uploading a module to the Git registry and consuming it on a container that is gracefully shut down); fix integration issues discovered across stories.",
      "most_likely_effort": 4
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A11",
      "activity_name": "Documentation, release notes, and final build verification",
      "activity_description": "Consolidate per-story documentation updates into the reference guide, write release notes summarizing the new behavior, run a final full build and test pass to produce the release artifacts.",
      "most_likely_effort": 2
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 51
  }
}
```

technical_and_design_decisions: U1: gpfdist sink will be moved to core with minimal refactoring; original code structure preserved to limit regression risk.

U2: Module registry will be backed by a Git repository (not the GitHub REST API) using simple clone/pull/push semantics executed by the admin and container nodes; admin acts as the writer, containers as the readers.

U3: Benchmark will use a representative mix of fan-in and fan-out streams to evaluate horizontal scaling when adding xd-container nodes; results will be published as an internal report rather than as new framework code.
U4: Flo parser endpoint improvements will follow a uniform error response envelope (HTTP status + machine-readable error code + human message) consistent with existing Spring XD REST APIs.

U5: Mail source SSL/TLS support will be implemented by passing through JavaMail Session properties (util:properties bean) into the existing Spring Integration mail adapter, avoiding custom SSL plumbing.

U6: HDFS becomes the default distributed remote location for the module registry; custom-modules.zip will be removed from the YARN distribution artifacts and replaced with a build-time note directing admins to upload via xd-shell/REST.

U7: xd-shell auto-configuration will be implemented via a documented init script location (e.g. /etc/springxd/conf/xd-shell.init) that is replayed at shell startup using the existing 'script' command.

U8: Graceful stream shutdown will be implemented by setting a configurable drain timeout on the message bus, then signalling modules to stop accepting new messages, and only stopping the container once the bus is drained or the timeout elapses.
assumptions: A single developer performs all the work (no team coordination overhead included beyond a self-review pass per activity).
One workday equals 8 hours of focused, uninterrupted development work.
The developer is already familiar with the Spring XD codebase, build system (Gradle), and existing test infrastructure, so ramp-up time is not estimated separately.
No large-scale refactoring or new architectural frameworks are introduced; each user story is a focused, additive change.
Each user story bundles design, implementation, unit tests, and integration tests, plus the minimum required documentation update; an extra global integration and release pass is added at the end.
Rackspace infrastructure for U3 is already provisioned or can be provisioned in a single setup pass; cost of the infrastructure itself is out of scope.
Test mail servers (plain and SSL/TLS-enabled IMAP/SMTP) are available locally or via freely accessible test accounts for U5.
The existing Flo parser service is a standalone web application whose endpoints can be modified without breaking the Flo UI.
HDFS is the only distributed remote location supported after U6; NFS-based distributed locations are out of scope.
Effort estimates cover development work only; they do not include code reviews by other developers, stakeholder meetings, or waiting time on external teams.
